title: Mark Your Calendars: These Are the Most Important Games of the 2026 NFL Season
contentHtml:
The 2026 NFL season will begin pro football anew tonight in, well, almost exactly the same way we left it last in February. The defending-champion Seattle Seahawks will face their Super Bowl LX foe, the New England Patriots, at 8:20 PM ET on NBC. That’s surprisingly rare — it’s only the third time the two previous Super Bowl teams have played in Week 1 of the following season, and only the second time ever (joining Panthers-Broncos from 2016) that it’s happened in the very first game on the schedule.

Subscribe now

Unlike that one — where Trevor Siemian started for Denver following Peyton Manning’s retirement — this version will actually feature the same QBs from seven months earlier, in Sam Darnold and Drake Maye, plus a number of familiar names and faces from last year’s playoffs and beyond. It should tell us something about each team as repeat Super Bowl contenders, since both will struggle to fight regression after seasons where a lot went right (while a lot went wrong for their rivals).

But how important does that make the game itself? We can begin to answer that question about tonight’s matchup, and indeed any matchup on the 2026 calendar, by dusting off a recurring feature here that I’m going to add permanently among all the goodies on my 2025 NFL tracker page: game-by-game leverage for each team’s odds of making the playoffs and/or winning the Super Bowl.
